data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 argues against decentralization by positing 'Cascading Correlation' via load-shifting, but its own countercondition concedes the same cascade can occur in the large service when its load balancer becomes the bottleneck. It then gives no causal reason why the decentralized path is worse when the centralized path has an equivalent, explicitly listed cascade mechanism. Since the problem's comparison is specifically against a large service with strictly more total internal redundancy, an argument that identifies a shared failure mode but does not establish which architecture is more vulnerable to it fails to resolve the claim in either direction; the mechanism is symmetric and thus non-discriminating.
